meta.wind_source: Global Renewables Watch, Microsoft AI for Good and The Nature Conservancy, MIT
meta.note: Satellite-derived. constructed_before is when the array was first seen COMPLETE, not a commercial operation date - Grootfontein was complete Dec 2024 and reached COD Dec 2025.
meta.wind_note: Wind is application-level clustered to farms at a 5 km radius - GRW maps individual turbines, not footprints, so there is no polygon to group by. turbines is the count within 10 km of the authorisation point; claimed is authorised MW summed across the applications pointing at that farm, which overstates where phases overlap.
meta.turbine_count_caveat: Per-farm turbine counts sum to 2233 against 1,472 in GRW nationally. The count is turbines within 10 km of an authorisation point, so adjacent farms share them. Usable for sizing a map marker, not as a capacity figure.
meta.licence: DERIVED DATA UNDER MIXED TERMS - not the CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 that covers GridTwin's own files, and the difference matters.
meta.licence_solar: Solar geometry and capacity derive from TransitionZero's Solar Asset Mapper, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Attribution to TransitionZero required, NON-COMMERCIAL use only, and changes must be stated - they are: polygons reduced to centroids, capacity carried through unchanged, and REEA authorisations matched within 10 km.
meta.licence_wind: Wind locations derive from Global Renewables Watch, Microsoft AI for Good with The Nature Conservancy, MIT licence. No commercial restriction.
meta.licence_consequence: The solar half cannot go into a commercial product. If that is ever needed, the wind half is clean and the solar would have to be rebuilt from GRW alone - which ends Q2 2024 and would lose every array completed since.

meta.naming: Names DERIVED from REEA authorisation text, not from a register - South Africa publishes no project-name-to-location mapping. Method: for each array, score every word used by authorisations within 10 km by local frequency times log(national rarity), and take the top word above a 1.5 threshold. That surfaces place names and suppresses generic terms without a stopword list, because "facility" appears in a thousand authorisations and scores near zero. A short blocklist removes the generic words that were locally distinctive anyway. NOT AUTHORITATIVE. These are the place an array sits near, inferred from paperwork - "Kathu" and "Kenhardt" are right, but a name is a lead to verify, not a fact. name_score is retained so a weak inference is visible.
meta.naming_licence: Derived from REEA authorisation text, public government data, so it adds no licence obligation. The OpenStreetMap route was rejected for two reasons: the Dunnett 2020 dataset predates every array completed since 2020, and OSM-derived data must be redistributed under ODbL share-alike, which is incompatible with the CC BY-NC-ND on GridTwin files and would have stacked a second conflicting obligation on top of TZ-SAM non-commercial.
meta.extent: SOUTH AFRICA ONLY. The Earth Engine scripts now filter on FAO GAUL level 0 rather than a bounding box. This file was additionally cleaned of five assets - four Namibian, one Lesothan, 174 MW - that the old rectangle [16,-35,33,-22] had let in. That box takes in southern Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini and slices of Botswana and Mozambique, and it was used in every count produced on 12 Sep 2026 before this was caught. The interim clean here is coarse geometry; the authoritative filter is the GAUL boundary in the scripts.
